title: Return of the Australian Trio
summary: Amelia Besseny, Cooper Bowman and Yuta Matsumura revisit the group’s earlier records and discuss their free-form approach, trip-hop atmosphere and changing creative chemistry.
transcript:
Amelia Besseny, Cooper Bowman and Yuta Matsumura of Th Blisks joined Lauren Taylor and Simon Winkler in the Triple R studios, ahead of their show at Miscellania for Efficient Space's 10th anniversary. Broadcast on Breaking and Entering, Triple R, 29 January 2026.

Host: We are joined in studio by all three members of the trio, Th Blisks. Is this the first time you've, I don't know, all been in a radio studio together? I can imagine it would be.

Guest: Yeah. We're spread out across Australia.

Host: We've got Cooper Bowman, Amelia Besseny and Yuta Matsumura joining us. Thanks so much for being here and having a chat with us ahead of your show tomorrow night, celebrating 10 years of the incredible Efficient Space label at Miscellania.

Host: Listeners to RRR would be very familiar with all of your projects, of course, individually and collectively, so highly prolific and accomplished across various creative disciplines, music, academic and otherwise. Bands from yourself, Yuta, like Low Life, Oily Boys.

You've been working with Keanu Nelson, of course, absolute legends. And Cooper running Altered States Tapes, now out of Hobart, a label which started all the way back in 2010, now past its 100th release. And Amelia Besseny, of course, an incredible academic and music maker, classically trained. Cooper and Amelia making music together as Troth. But at some point, Yuta, apparently you invited all three of you to make something a little bit different as Th Blisks. Is that right?

Yuta: Yeah, that's right.

Host: What was the catalyst? What was the moment that made you think, 'I think we can do something together'?

Yuta: I think at the time, Cooper and I were hanging out with each other a lot. I was going up to Newcastle, I think it was back in 2019 or something. [Unclear audio at 00:01:46–00:01:49] And I guess after a few long nights of talking about music, it just felt right to ask him and Amelia to have a jam together and make some weirdo, whatever you'd call it, trip-hop at the time. I don't like to call it trip-hop, but at the time I was playing around with slowing down jungle beats, and I thought I might test that and see what Cooper can do and Amelia can do as well.

Host: So there wasn't necessarily a clear kind of concept?

Yuta: No, it wasn't a clear decision. I mean, the first recording we did, we did like three songs in a day off that first record, pretty much. You guys came over, I think.

Guest: Yeah, we came right to yours.

Host: What was that first day like?

Guest: We were hung over. I think those three songs were 'Garfitti'. Yeah, 'Taipei Dubble', all the slow ones. Gives a sense of where we were at.

Host: You were soundtracking the mood.

Guest: Yeah, so we evolved organically after that, and then we did that album pretty quickly. It was good. We didn't have any expectations, I think, when we went to play the songs and then ended up recording a few. It was like, cool, we can do it together. So yeah, it was nice.

[Unclear audio at 00:03:10–00:03:12]

Host: And I guess, how do you see Th Blisks in relation to your other projects? Because I guess maybe Yuta, your solo work, and Cooper and Amelia, your work with Troth.

[Unclear audio at 00:03:20–00:03:22]

Cooper: I mean, I guess it's kind of hard. Sometimes the lines get blurred, because Amelia has a pretty distinctive voice and we have those same interests come out in what you're doing. But you try and keep the things distinct. And I mean, it's always going to be different with three people involved. It's more of a conversation. So you just try and keep that element, that vitality to it. What do you reckon, Yuta?

Yuta: Yeah, I think that's right. [Unclear audio at 00:03:48–00:03:51] Obviously, there's similarities across all three of our projects. But I think when we're all together making something, it stands out. It's unique compared to — I don't know. I think what we do individually is unique as well. But to me, it's all different.

Cooper: Yeah, and you've got to keep it different. I mean, there's more chaos, I guess. Yuta and I especially have pretty different perspectives on things, which comes out, in a way, in what you do.

Host: And that's a good thing, though, right?

Guest: It's different chemistries across different projects and stuff. So naturally, you're going to get different sounds.

Host: You were laughing about that idea of the differences of opinions. Would that be an example of maybe a perspective?

Guest: Oh, you want some drama?

[Unclear audio at 00:04:38–00:04:41]

Yuta: Well, I think the way we approach writing music is a lot different. Maybe I'm a bit more chaotic in that sense, a bit more free, but also particular. And I think Cooper — I don't know, you can talk for yourself.

Cooper: No, no, no, go on, go on. Don't tell me.

[Unclear audio at 00:05:05–00:05:07]

Yuta: No, I think what you do is you pull samples from a library, and that's a very kind of librarian mentality. When I go into a library, I just go, 'Oh, what's this like? I'm just going to chuck this together.'

Cooper: Yeah. Maybe it's a bit more considered, and that can be a limitation or it can be a strength.

Yuta: No, I think it's both. And same for me, there's weaknesses. So we hopefully meet in the middle.

[Unclear audio at 00:05:40–00:05:44]

Yuta: Amelia's approach is also quite fluid. And I think it's quite ethereal on top of this chaos that Cooper and I have. So it binds really nicely.

[Unclear audio at 00:06:06–00:06:08]

Host: You're playing at Miscellania this Friday, chapter one of Efficient Space's 10th anniversary series of performances and sets. We have the chance also to celebrate and revisit How So?, which is the debut of Th Blisks. You were talking a little bit before about that momentous first day where the first three songs came into being.

But we'd love to talk to you a bit more about that album and how it feels to see it have a second chapter now on Efficient Space. Maybe, Amelia, how does it feel?

[Unclear audio at 00:06:46–00:06:48]

Amelia: Well, I think it's great. And luckily the records came just in time for the show as well, which is always nice. It's a Blisks miracle.

[Unclear audio at 00:06:55–00:06:58]

Guest: It is. When we've played shows as Troth, we've actually had people come up to us overseas, pointing at pictures on their phone, being like, 'This record, make this one again.' And we're like, 'Oh, we'll have to talk to you about that.'

Host: Because there were 150 copies and that was it. Is that right?

Guest: Yeah. Initially. On Altered States originally.

Host: I suppose with the songs themselves, has your relationship to the tracks changed over time? Do you hear anything in it now that you perhaps didn't at the time? Maybe for yourself, Cooper?

Cooper: Well, we jammed last week. Yuta came down to Hobart and we played through the songs properly for kind of the first time for some of them. And so you're hearing them in a different light completely than doing them. And I think it was kind of exciting to play them, because they take on a new life.

And I hope they're on the right side of looseness. Hopefully that spirit is in them. So it changes over time. If you're playing them for the first time years later, it's kind of like an exciting experience more than anything, which is really nice. But yeah, just even hearing them again, I'm proud of that record. I think it still stands up a few years later.

Guest: It felt great to play some of the songs together live.

Host: We're looking forward to experiencing that, that emotion and I guess the magic of you three together, tomorrow for sure. And your most recent album, Elixa, that we just heard a track from before, made across three very different locations. I think Cooper and Amelia, you were in Newcastle and then Hobart. You were out in Papunya for a couple of years.

You've described that process as a call and response, rather than the immediacy of being in a room together. What were you actually sending back and forth to each other?

[Unclear audio at 00:08:48–00:08:51]

Guest: You'd have just been like, 'Nah, that's wrong.'

[Unclear audio at 00:08:52–00:08:54]

Guest: That's what you were saying.

Yuta: No, you guys gang up on me. [Unclear audio at 00:08:58–00:09:01] 'Amelia and I don't reckon this is good.' And I'm like, 'I want to hear Amelia say that.' [Unclear audio] Amelia's too nice.

[Unclear audio at 00:09:07–00:09:10]

Guest: Just a lot of emails.

[Unclear audio at 00:09:11–00:09:13]

Guest: It's hard because you don't have the immediacy of conversation, because if you were together, you'd probably figure it out quicker. So it takes longer. And I think we'd made the pictures for the album before anything, maybe, too. I don't know.

Guest: Yeah, maybe. So there was a kind of visual language. The rock faces, yeah.

Guest: Oh, no, this is for Elixa, like the one we did by correspondence.

Guest: Oh, that was, yes. That was Oscar stuff.

Guest: Yeah, shout out to Oscar for the cover of that. It's a good cover.

Guest: I feel like that encapsulates what we're doing, though. It's kind of cartoonish in a sense. I don't know.

[Unclear audio at 00:10:04–00:19:19]
